description: Tool execution happens only if the ticket is valid, the tool is granted and registered, the arguments are validated, the resources are granted and the call limit is not used up
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (g_execute_called => ((g_ticket_found & g_ticket_bound & !g_ticket_expired) & (g_tool_granted & g_tool_registered) & g_args_valid & g_resources_in_grants & g_budget_left))

description: If all the above conditions hold and the argument shape, content policy and order rules also pass, the call executes
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy ((((g_ticket_found & g_ticket_bound & !g_ticket_expired) & (g_tool_granted & g_tool_registered) & g_args_valid & g_resources_in_grants & g_budget_left) & g_args_shape_ok & g_content_ok & g_sequence_ok) => g_execute_called)

description: If the ticket is missing, belongs to another turn or has expired, the call is denied and no tool code is called
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy ((!g_ticket_found | !g_ticket_bound | g_ticket_expired) => (g_permission_denied & !g_validate_called & !g_resources_called & !g_execute_called))

description: A tool that is not granted or not registered is denied and no tool code is called
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (((g_ticket_found & g_ticket_bound & !g_ticket_expired) & (!g_tool_granted | !g_tool_registered)) => (g_permission_denied & !g_validate_called & !g_resources_called & !g_execute_called))

description: validate is called only if the ticket is valid and the tool is granted. In that case it is called if the argument shape is correct
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy ((g_validate_called => ((g_ticket_found & g_ticket_bound & !g_ticket_expired) & (g_tool_granted & g_tool_registered))) & (((g_ticket_found & g_ticket_bound & !g_ticket_expired) & (g_tool_granted & g_tool_registered) & g_args_shape_ok) => g_validate_called))

description: resources is computed only from arguments that passed validation
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (g_resources_called <=> (g_validate_called & g_args_valid))

description: If the resources leave the granted scope, the call is denied and the call count is not used
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy ((g_resources_called & !g_resources_in_grants) => (g_permission_denied & !g_counter_incremented & !g_execute_called))

description: If the call limit is used up, the call is denied
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy ((g_resources_called & g_resources_in_grants & !g_budget_left) => (g_permission_denied & !g_counter_incremented & !g_execute_called))

description: The call count is used just before execution. It is not given back if the tool fails
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (g_counter_incremented <=> g_execute_called)

description: PermissionError is raised only on a denial condition (ticket, tool grant, argument shape, resources, call limit, content policy, order rules), and is always raised on an original denial condition (ticket, tool grant, resources, call limit)
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy ((g_permission_denied => (!(g_ticket_found & g_ticket_bound & !g_ticket_expired) | !(g_tool_granted & g_tool_registered) | !g_args_shape_ok | (g_resources_called & (!g_resources_in_grants | !g_budget_left | !g_content_ok | !g_sequence_ok)))) & ((!(g_ticket_found & g_ticket_bound & !g_ticket_expired) | !(g_tool_granted & g_tool_registered) | (g_resources_called & (!g_resources_in_grants | !g_budget_left))) => g_permission_denied))

description: Exceptions of tool code (validate, execute) are propagated unchanged
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (g_tool_error <=> ((g_validate_called & !g_args_valid) | (g_execute_called & g_execute_fails)))

description: If execution succeeds, the result is returned
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (g_result_returned <=> (g_execute_called & !g_execute_fails))

description: The outcome of one call is exactly one of denial, tool error and success
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (((g_permission_denied | g_tool_error) | g_result_returned) & !(g_permission_denied & g_tool_error) & !(g_permission_denied & g_result_returned) & !(g_tool_error & g_result_returned))

description: validate receives a copy of the arguments, so the caller's arguments do not change
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (g_validate_called => g_args_copied)

description: The arguments used for the check and for the execution are the same object (no gap between check time and use time)
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (g_execute_called => g_same_checked_args)

description: The gate does not change the permissions, expiry or limit of the ticket
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (!g_ticket_changed)

asis_note: The original passes the arguments to the tool's validate without looking at their shape. The shape check is left to the tool code
description: If the argument shape is wrong (not a JSON object, or it breaks the parameter schema of the tool or the size and depth limits), the call is denied and no tool code is called
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (!g_args_shape_ok => (g_permission_denied & !g_validate_called & !g_resources_called & !g_execute_called))

asis_note: The original has no place for a content policy. If the resources are inside the granted scope, it executes whatever the content of the arguments
description: A call that the operator's content policy blocks is not executed and does not use the call count
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy ((g_resources_called & !g_content_ok) => (g_permission_denied & !g_counter_incremented & !g_execute_called))

asis_note: The original has no call order rules. Whatever calls came before, it executes if the call is inside the granted scope
description: A call that the order rules block is not executed and does not use the call count
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy ((g_resources_called & !g_sequence_ok) => (g_permission_denied & !g_counter_incremented & !g_execute_called))

asis_note: The original has none of the three checks
description: Tool execution happens only if the argument shape, the content policy and the order rules all pass (extension of GATE-01)
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (g_execute_called => (g_args_shape_ok & g_content_ok & g_sequence_ok))

asis_note: The original keeps no order record of executed calls
description: Every executed call, and only an executed call, is written to the order record (basis of the order rules and of the completion evidence)
fretish: Gate shall always satisfy (g_call_recorded <=> g_execute_called)

description: revoke removes the ticket, its call count and the ticket link of the context
fretish: Ticket shall always satisfy (t_revoke_requested => (t_ticket_removed & t_counter_removed & t_context_cleared))

description: Revoking a ticket that does not exist raises no error (calling it twice is safe)
fretish: Ticket shall always satisfy ((t_revoke_requested & !t_ticket_present) => !t_error)

description: An issued ticket object is immutable (frozen dataclass)
fretish: Ticket shall always satisfy (!t_ticket_mutated_in_place)

description: A ticket always has task_id, session_id, an expiry time and a call limit
fretish: Ticket shall always satisfy (t_binding_fields_present & t_has_expiry & t_has_call_budget)

description: If there is no plan, the stage fails with a reason and does not call the LLM
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy (!a_plan_present => (a_result_failed & a_message_nonempty & !a_verifier_called & !a_ticket_issued))

description: If the verification LLM fails or its output has a wrong format, no ticket is issued (fail closed)
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy ((a_plan_present & a_verifier_error) => (a_error_propagated & !a_ticket_issued))

description: If a tool that is not registered is approved, the stage fails without a ticket
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy (((a_plan_present & !a_verifier_error) & a_any_unknown_tool) => (a_result_failed & a_message_nonempty & !a_ticket_issued))

description: If a tool that is not in the permission table is approved, the stage fails without a ticket (default deny)
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy (((a_plan_present & !a_verifier_error) & a_any_scope_missing) => (a_result_failed & a_message_nonempty & !a_ticket_issued))

description: If even one approval leaves the policy (intersection of agent and user permissions), the whole is denied without partial issue
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy (((a_plan_present & !a_verifier_error) & a_any_exceeds_policy) => (a_result_failed & a_message_nonempty & !a_ticket_issued))

asis_note: The original passes only the policy check, without restriction to the plan, so it issues a ticket even when only approvals outside the plan remain
description: If there are tool steps but no usable approval, the stage fails with a reason
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy ((((a_plan_present & !a_verifier_error) & !a_any_unknown_tool & !a_any_scope_missing & !a_any_exceeds_policy) & a_plan_has_tool_steps & a_usable_empty) => (a_result_failed & a_message_nonempty & !a_ticket_issued))

description: If all checks pass, a ticket is issued and the turn goes to EXECUTE (an empty ticket without permissions if there are no tool steps)
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy ((((a_plan_present & !a_verifier_error) & !a_any_unknown_tool & !a_any_scope_missing & !a_any_exceeds_policy) & !(a_plan_has_tool_steps & a_usable_empty)) => (a_ticket_issued & a_result_execute))

description: The issued ticket does not exceed the policy intersection
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy (!a_issued_beyond_policy)

description: The issued ticket does not exceed what the verification LLM approved (the LLM can only reduce)
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy (!a_issued_beyond_verifier)

asis_note: The original does not check that an approval is inside the plan (it issues the ticket as long as it is inside the policy)
description: The issued ticket is inside the tools and resources the plan requested (least privilege)
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy (!a_issued_outside_plan)

asis_note: The original has no cutting step
description: If there are approvals outside the plan, they are cut off before issuing
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy ((a_ticket_issued & a_any_outside_plan) => a_grants_trimmed)

description: The ticket is bound to this turn (session_id and task_id), has an expiry time and a call limit, is stored under a new unique id, and its call count starts at 0
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy (a_ticket_issued => (a_ticket_bound_to_task & a_ticket_has_expiry & a_ticket_has_call_budget & a_ticket_id_fresh & a_ticket_stored & a_counter_zero))

description: Going to EXECUTE and issuing a ticket are the same thing
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy (a_result_execute <=> a_ticket_issued)

description: The verification LLM is called only if there is a plan, at most once
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy ((a_verifier_called <=> a_plan_present) & (a_llm_calls <= 1) & ((a_llm_calls = 1) <=> a_verifier_called))

description: The verification LLM receives only the items the plan requested, the objective and the list of registered tools
fretish: Authorizer shall always satisfy (a_verifier_called => a_request_from_plan_only)

description: If the analysis call limit (3 per turn) is used up, the stage ends with LIMIT_REACHED without calling the LLM
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (!n_budget_left => (n_next = ST_LIMIT & n_llm_calls = 0 & !n_counter_incremented & !n_plan_created & !n_error_propagated))

description: Starting an analysis uses one call count
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (n_budget_left => n_counter_incremented)

description: One analysis makes at most two LLM calls (including the re-analysis after a recall)
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (n_llm_calls <= 2)

description: If the action is respond, the turn completes with the LLM's answer and no plan
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (((n_budget_left & !n_error) & n_action = ACT_RESPOND) => (n_next = ST_COMPLETED & n_message_from_llm & !n_plan_created & n_llm_calls = 1 & !n_error_propagated))

description: If the action is clarify, the turn waits for user input
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (((n_budget_left & !n_error) & n_action = ACT_CLARIFY) => (n_next = ST_WAITING & n_message_from_llm & !n_plan_created & n_llm_calls = 1 & !n_error_propagated))

description: If the action is history, the recall ids are recorded and the analysis runs once more
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (((n_budget_left & !n_error) & n_action = ACT_HISTORY) => (n_llm_calls = 2 & n_recall_recorded))

description: If the second response after a recall is respond, the turn completes
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (((n_budget_left & !n_error) & n_action = ACT_HISTORY & n_action2 = ACT_RESPOND) => (n_next = ST_COMPLETED & n_message_from_llm & !n_plan_created & !n_error_propagated))

description: If the second response after a recall is clarify, the turn waits
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (((n_budget_left & !n_error) & n_action = ACT_HISTORY & n_action2 = ACT_CLARIFY) => (n_next = ST_WAITING & n_message_from_llm & !n_plan_created & !n_error_propagated))

description: Any other response creates and stores a plan and goes to authorization (the content of the plan is not validated)
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (((n_budget_left & !n_error) & (n_action = ACT_PLAN | (n_action = ACT_HISTORY & n_action2 != ACT_RESPOND & n_action2 != ACT_CLARIFY))) => (n_plan_created & n_context_updated & n_next = ST_AUTHORIZE & !n_error_propagated))

description: On the plan path, the LLM is called only once for the first response
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (((n_budget_left & !n_error) & n_action = ACT_PLAN) => n_llm_calls = 1)

description: An LLM error or a format error creates no plan and is raised (fail closed)
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy ((n_budget_left & n_error) => (n_error_propagated & !n_plan_created))

description: The analysis stage neither creates nor changes a ticket and executes no tool
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy (!n_ticket_touched & !n_tool_executed)

description: The analysis LLM receives only the latest user entry and the list of registered tools
fretish: Analyzer shall always satisfy ((n_llm_calls >= 1) => n_input_from_history_and_registry)

description: If there is no valid ticket, neither the LLM nor a tool is called, and the stage raises an error (original), returns to authorization or ends with failure (guard)
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy (!x_ticket_valid => ((x_error_propagated | x_next = ST_AUTHORIZE | x_next = ST_FAILED) & !x_llm_called & !x_gate_invoked))

description: The worker LLM is called only if the ticket is valid and call limit is left
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy (x_llm_called <=> (x_ticket_valid & x_worker_budget_left))

description: The worker LLM is shown only the schemas of the tools the ticket grants
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy (x_llm_called => x_schemas_only_granted)

description: If the worker LLM call limit (8 per turn) is used up, the stage ends with LIMIT_REACHED
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy ((x_ticket_valid & !x_worker_budget_left) => (x_next = ST_LIMIT & !x_error_propagated & !x_gate_invoked))

description: If there are no tool calls, the work result is recorded and the turn goes to evaluation
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy (((x_ticket_valid & x_worker_budget_left) & !x_llm_error & !x_worker_calls_tools) => (x_next = ST_EVALUATE & x_work_result_recorded & !x_error_propagated & !x_gate_invoked))

description: If the calls requested at once exceed the tool call limit (12 per turn), none is executed and the stage ends with LIMIT_REACHED
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy (((x_ticket_valid & x_worker_budget_left) & !x_llm_error & x_worker_calls_tools & x_batch_exceeds_budget) => (x_next = ST_LIMIT & !x_error_propagated & !x_gate_invoked))

description: A worker LLM error calls no tool and is raised
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy (((x_ticket_valid & x_worker_budget_left) & x_llm_error) => (x_error_propagated & !x_gate_invoked))

description: The gate is called only for calls in a batch within the limit whose arguments parse
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy (x_gate_invoked <=> (((x_ticket_valid & x_worker_budget_left) & !x_llm_error & x_worker_calls_tools & !x_batch_exceeds_budget) & x_args_parse_ok))

description: If the tool arguments are not JSON, the call does not go to the gate and an error is raised
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy ((((x_ticket_valid & x_worker_budget_left) & !x_llm_error & x_worker_calls_tools & !x_batch_exceeds_budget) & !x_args_parse_ok) => (x_error_propagated & !x_gate_invoked))

description: Every tool call attempt is recorded in the history before going to the gate and counted in the attempts (including denied attempts)
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy (x_gate_invoked => (x_call_recorded_before_gate & x_attempt_counted))

description: If a tool fails or is denied, only the exception type (error_type) is recorded for the LLM, the remaining calls are not executed and the error is raised
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy ((x_gate_invoked & (x_gate_outcome != GO_OK | !x_result_serializable)) => (x_error_type_only & x_error_propagated & x_later_calls_skipped))

description: A successful call records its result and the stage continues
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy ((x_gate_invoked & x_gate_outcome = GO_OK & x_result_serializable) => (x_result_recorded & !x_error_propagated))

description: Text that accompanies a tool call is recorded as an assistant entry before the call is executed
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy ((((x_ticket_valid & x_worker_budget_left) & !x_llm_error & x_worker_calls_tools & !x_batch_exceeds_budget) & x_worker_text_present) => x_interim_text_recorded)

description: The execute of a tool runs only through the gate (_execute_tool) (complete mediation)
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy (!x_tool_run_outside_gate)

asis_note: If json.loads fails, the original raises an exception before add_tool_call, so it neither records nor counts this attempt (O-02)
description: An attempt with unparsable arguments is also recorded in the history and counted in the attempts (no audit gap)
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy ((((x_ticket_valid & x_worker_budget_left) & !x_llm_error & x_worker_calls_tools & !x_batch_exceeds_budget) & !x_args_parse_ok) => (x_malformed_recorded & x_attempt_counted))

asis_note: The original puts a tool result into the history whatever its size and sends it again with every later LLM call
description: A tool result over the limit is cut before it is recorded (bounds the size and cost of the LLM input)
fretish: Executor shall always satisfy (((x_gate_invoked & x_gate_outcome = GO_OK & x_result_serializable) & x_result_oversize) => (x_result_truncated & x_result_recorded))

description: The evaluation stage calls the LLM exactly once
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy (v_llm_calls = 1)

description: An LLM error or a format error is raised
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy (v_llm_error => v_error_propagated)

description: If completed and there is evidence, the turn completes (the message becomes the final answer)
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy ((!v_llm_error & v_message_present & v_decision = DEC_COMPLETED & v_evidence_ok) => (v_next = ST_COMPLETED & v_message_is_llm_text & !v_error_propagated))

description: If execute, further execution runs with the same ticket
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy ((!v_llm_error & v_message_present & v_decision = DEC_EXECUTE) => (v_next = ST_EXECUTE & v_message_is_llm_text & !v_error_propagated))

description: If authorize, the turn returns to the authorization stage and gets a new ticket (the policy check runs again)
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy ((!v_llm_error & v_message_present & v_decision = DEC_AUTHORIZE) => (v_next = ST_AUTHORIZE & v_message_is_llm_text & !v_error_propagated))

description: If analyze, the turn starts again from analysis
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy ((!v_llm_error & v_message_present & v_decision = DEC_ANALYZE) => (v_next = ST_ANALYZE & v_message_is_llm_text & !v_error_propagated))

description: If ask, the turn waits for user input
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy ((!v_llm_error & v_message_present & v_decision = DEC_ASK) => (v_next = ST_WAITING & v_message_is_llm_text & !v_error_propagated))

description: If failed, the turn ends with failure
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy ((!v_llm_error & v_message_present & v_decision = DEC_FAILED) => (v_next = ST_FAILED & v_message_is_llm_text & !v_error_propagated))

description: An unknown decision value or a response without message is not treated as completion; it becomes an error and the same stage is tried again
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy ((!v_llm_error & (!(v_decision = DEC_COMPLETED | v_decision = DEC_EXECUTE | v_decision = DEC_AUTHORIZE | v_decision = DEC_ANALYZE | v_decision = DEC_ASK | v_decision = DEC_FAILED) | !v_message_present)) => v_error_propagated)

description: The evaluation stage neither creates nor changes a ticket and executes no tool
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy (!v_ticket_touched & !v_tool_executed)

asis_note: If the evaluation LLM says completed, the original treats the turn as complete even if no tool was ever executed (O-05)
description: If the plan required a tool and the gate executed no call successfully, the turn is not treated as complete even if the LLM says completed; it is sent to further execution or to failure
fretish: Evaluator shall always satisfy ((!v_llm_error & v_message_present & v_decision = DEC_COMPLETED & !v_evidence_ok) => ((v_next = ST_EXECUTE | v_next = ST_FAILED) & !v_error_propagated))

description: When a turn starts, the instruction is recorded in the history first
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy (r_turn_start => r_user_recorded)

description: If cancellation is requested, the turn ends with CANCELLED without calling a handler
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy (((r_state = ST_ANALYZE | r_state = ST_AUTHORIZE | r_state = ST_EXECUTE | r_state = ST_EVALUATE) & r_cancel) => (r_next_state = ST_CANCELLED & !r_handler_invoked))

description: When the step limit (max_steps) is reached, the turn ends with LIMIT_REACHED without calling a handler
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy (((r_state = ST_ANALYZE | r_state = ST_AUTHORIZE | r_state = ST_EXECUTE | r_state = ST_EVALUATE) & !r_cancel & r_steps_at_limit) => (r_next_state = ST_LIMIT & !r_handler_invoked))

description: Before the analysis and authorization handlers are called, the previous ticket is removed
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy ((r_handler_invoked & (r_state = ST_ANALYZE | r_state = ST_AUTHORIZE)) => r_ticket_revoked_before_handler)

description: A handler is called only if the state is active and there is neither cancellation nor limit
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy (r_handler_invoked <=> ((r_state = ST_ANALYZE | r_state = ST_AUTHORIZE | r_state = ST_EXECUTE | r_state = ST_EVALUATE) & !r_cancel & !r_steps_at_limit))

description: Every handler call (including a failing one) counts a step. So the iteration is bounded by max_steps
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy (r_handler_invoked => r_step_counted)

description: If a handler succeeds, its result is the next state
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy ((r_handler_invoked & !r_handler_raised) => (r_next_state = r_stage_next))

description: A handler exception makes the same stage be tried again, tells the LLM only the exception type and writes the details only to stderr
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy ((r_handler_invoked & r_handler_raised & !r_blocked_start) => (r_next_state = r_state & r_feedback_error_type_only & r_stderr_logged))

asis_note: The original treats every exception as a retry of the same stage, so with an expired ticket it loops in EXECUTE up to the maximum iterations (20) and ends with limit_reached
description: If execution cannot start because the ticket is missing or expired, the turn does not loop in the same stage; it returns to authorization or ends with failure
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy ((r_handler_invoked & r_handler_raised & r_blocked_start) => (r_next_state = ST_AUTHORIZE | r_next_state = ST_FAILED))

asis_note: The original ends LIMIT_REACHED and CANCELLED with an empty message
description: A turn that had a denial or a blocked start does not end with an empty message
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy ((r_exit & r_denial_seen) => r_message_nonempty_out)

description: The ticket is removed on whatever path the turn ends (finally)
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy (r_exit => r_ticket_revoked_at_exit)

description: The final message is appended as an assistant entry only if it differs from the last entry of the history
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy (r_message_appended <=> (r_exit & r_message_nonempty_out & !r_last_is_same_assistant))

asis_note: The original has no cost limit. Even in a situation that counts as over the limit it keeps calling the LLM until the step limit, and ends LIMIT_REACHED with an empty message
description: A turn whose LLM call was blocked by the cost limit does not end with an empty message and tells the user the reason
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy ((r_exit & r_budget_seen) => r_message_nonempty_out)

asis_note: The original has no usage totals
description: The usage totals return to 0 only when a turn starts (an earlier turn does not block the next one, and repeating a stage does not restart the limit)
fretish: Turn shall always satisfy (r_usage_reset <=> r_turn_start)

asis_note: The restore of the original (from_jsonl) accepts managed records of the stream as they are
description: Operator (managed) entries arise only through add_managed_prompt
fretish: History shall always satisfy (h_managed_entry_added => (h_op = OP_ADD_MANAGED))

asis_note: The original accepts them and puts them into the system prompt of every stage
description: Managed records of a restored stream are not accepted
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_RESTORE & h_record_kind_managed) => (!h_managed_entry_added & !h_entry_appended & h_record_rejected))

asis_note: The original accepts them and passes them to the worker LLM as genuine tool results
description: Tool_call and tool_result records of a restored stream are not accepted (the way a forged tool result reaches the worker LLM)
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_RESTORE & h_record_kind_tool) => (!h_tool_entry_added & !h_entry_appended & h_record_rejected))

asis_note: The original discards the session_id and merges all records into the session of the first record
description: Records with a session_id different from that of the first record are not accepted (prevents mixing of sessions)
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_RESTORE & h_record_foreign_session) => (!h_entry_appended & h_record_rejected))

asis_note: The original does not check kind (it accepts it, but it is ignored in the LLM messages)
description: A kind outside the five is not accepted
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_RESTORE & h_record_kind_unknown) => (!h_entry_appended & h_record_rejected))

description: entries is a deep copy, so the caller cannot change the history
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_ENTRIES) => h_returns_copy)

description: An add operation appends an entry (the operation determines the kind)
fretish: History shall always satisfy (((h_op = OP_ADD_MANAGED | h_op = OP_ADD_USER | h_op = OP_ADD_ASSISTANT | h_op = OP_ADD_TOOL_CALL | h_op = OP_ADD_TOOL_RESULT)) => h_entry_appended)

description: The arguments of a tool call are recorded as a deep copy, so later changes do not change the history
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_ADD_TOOL_CALL) => h_args_deep_copied)

description: Adding a user entry registers its turn_id
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_ADD_USER) => h_turn_registered)

description: next_turn_id is the maximum of the registered turn_ids + 1
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_NEXT_TURN) => h_next_turn_max_plus_one)

description: fork creates a new session_id and an independent copy
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_FORK) => (h_fork_new_session & h_fork_independent))

description: to_jsonl exports all entries in order with session_id and the derived task_id
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_EXPORT) => h_export_complete)

description: If a record is malformed, the restore is rejected with an error and no partially restored history is returned
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_RESTORE & h_record_malformed) => (h_error & !h_history_returned))

description: An empty stream is an error
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_RESTORE & h_stream_empty) => (h_error & !h_history_returned))

description: Valid records are restored in order
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_RESTORE & !h_record_kind_managed & !h_record_kind_tool & !h_record_foreign_session & !h_record_kind_unknown & !h_record_malformed & !h_stream_empty) => (h_entry_appended & h_history_returned))

description: add_managed_prompt creates a managed entry (the only path the operator writes)
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_ADD_MANAGED) => h_managed_entry_added)

description: add_tool_call and add_tool_result create tool record entries (the only path the Core writes)
fretish: History shall always satisfy (((h_op = OP_ADD_TOOL_CALL | h_op = OP_ADD_TOOL_RESULT)) => h_tool_entry_added)

description: A new history is empty and has one session_id (session_id is read-only)
fretish: History shall always satisfy ((h_op = OP_CREATE) => (h_history_empty & h_session_fixed))

description: task_id is built only as session_id:turn_id and the caller cannot specify it
fretish: Instruction shall always satisfy ((i_op = IOP_CONSTRUCT) => i_task_id_derived)

description: If a stream record contains task_id, it is rejected
fretish: Instruction shall always satisfy ((i_op = IOP_PARSE & !i_line_blank & i_record_has_task_id) => (i_error & !i_instruction_yielded))

description: If a required key is missing or an unknown key is present, it is rejected
fretish: Instruction shall always satisfy ((i_op = IOP_PARSE & !i_line_blank & i_record_malformed) => (i_error & !i_instruction_yielded))

description: Blank lines are skipped
fretish: Instruction shall always satisfy ((i_op = IOP_PARSE & i_line_blank) => (!i_instruction_yielded & !i_error))

description: A valid record becomes an instruction object
fretish: Instruction shall always satisfy ((i_op = IOP_PARSE & !i_line_blank & !i_record_has_task_id & !i_record_malformed) => (i_instruction_yielded & !i_error))

description: UserInstruction is immutable (frozen)
fretish: Instruction shall always satisfy (!i_mutable_after_creation)

description: The permission table is deep-copied at construction, so later changes by the caller do not widen the policy
fretish: Config shall always satisfy (c_caller_mutates_policy_later => !c_policy_widened)

description: The tool registry is copied at construction, so later changes by the caller do not change the registration
fretish: Config shall always satisfy (c_caller_mutates_tools_later => !c_registry_changed)

description: Default limits: analysis 3, worker 8, tools 12, ticket validity 300 seconds
fretish: Config shall always satisfy (c_use_defaults => (c_max_analysis = 3 & c_max_worker = 8 & c_max_tools = 12 & c_ttl = 300))

description: Right after construction there is no ticket
fretish: Config shall always satisfy (c_construct => !c_ticket_exists_after)

description: If no permission table is given, no tool is authorized (default deny)
fretish: Config shall always satisfy ((c_construct & c_no_permissions_given) => !c_any_grant_possible)

description: LLM output is read only as JSON data and never executed or evaluated (only json.loads is used)
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy (!l_output_executed)

description: If json_output is not set, the response is returned unchanged
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_CALL & !l_json_requested & !l_budget_over) => l_response_passthrough)

description: If it is JSON, it is read and returned
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_CALL & l_json_requested & l_output_valid_json & !l_budget_over) => (l_json_parsed & !l_error_propagated))

description: If it is not JSON, it is raised as an error (it does not fall back to a default)
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_CALL & l_json_requested & !l_output_valid_json) => l_error_propagated)

description: The system prompt of every stage contains all managed entries of the history
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_SYSTEM) => l_managed_in_system_prompt)

description: Managed entries are not sent as conversation messages (they are only in the system prompt)
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_MESSAGES & l_entry_kind = KIND_MANAGED) => !l_msg_emitted)

description: User entries are sent in the user role
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_MESSAGES & l_entry_kind = KIND_USER) => (l_msg_emitted & l_role = ROLE_USER))

description: Assistant and tool_call entries are sent in the assistant role
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_MESSAGES & (l_entry_kind = KIND_ASSISTANT | l_entry_kind = KIND_TOOL_CALL)) => (l_msg_emitted & l_role = ROLE_ASSISTANT))

description: Tool results are always sent in the tool role (data) and never raised to the system prompt
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_MESSAGES & l_entry_kind = KIND_TOOL_RESULT) => (l_msg_emitted & l_role = ROLE_TOOL))

asis_note: The original has no cost limit. It calls the provider whatever the number of calls and the input size
description: An LLM call that exceeds the cost limit is not sent to the provider and is raised as an error
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_CALL & l_budget_over) => (!l_provider_called & l_error_propagated))

asis_note: The original does not count the size of a call
description: A call that reached the provider adds its input and output size to the usage of the turn (basis of the limit)
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_CALL & l_provider_called) => l_usage_recorded)

description: A call within the limit is sent to the provider (it is not blocked without reason)
fretish: LlmIO shall always satisfy ((l_op = LOP_CALL & !l_budget_over) => l_provider_called)

description: TaskRecord, ProcessingResult, ConversationEntry, PlannedStep, TaskPlan, StageResult, TurnResult and ToolDefinition are frozen and do not change after creation
fretish: Data shall always satisfy (!d_record_mutated_in_place)

description: There are only nine turn states (ANALYZE, AUTHORIZE, EXECUTE, EVALUATE, COMPLETED, WAITING_FOR_USER, CANCELLED, FAILED, LIMIT_REACHED)
fretish: Data shall always satisfy (d_state_count = 9)

description: TurnContext (counters, plan and ticket link) is created anew for every turn
fretish: Data shall always satisfy (d_context_new_per_turn)
